Regulator opens consultation on data portability rules

By Alec Fenwick14 May 2026

The regulator has opened a twelve-week consultation on how data portability obligations should apply to platforms above the designated user threshold. The document runs to sixty-one pages and closes to responses on 4 August.

Three proposals sit at its centre. The first would require an export format that is machine readable without vendor-specific tooling. The second sets a maximum fulfilment window of seven days for automated requests. The third, which industry bodies have already described as the most demanding, would extend the obligation to derived data as well as data the user supplied directly.

A spokesperson for the regulator said the consultation was deliberately broad and that no decision had been taken on any of the three. Responses will be published alongside a summary in the autumn.
